lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter heading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Chapter title. Leave a clean beat before story begins.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek woke with the taste of black water still in his mouth.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It was brackish and heavy. He sat upright on the narrow pallet, breathing through his nose while the taste clung to the back of his throat. The room was small, hot, and familiar. A cracked clay basin sat beside the wall. His boots were where he had left them. The thin curtain over the window stirred once and fell still.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The dream had been short. Darkness with weight. Pressure against his chest. A voice calling him by a name he had never heard.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He swung his feet to the floor and stood. Through the window the city lay under morning fog, its black spires jutting upward like jagged teeth. Ordinary sounds reached him—a cart on uneven stone, a woman shouting, a dog that barked once and went silent.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek turned to the bedside table. His father's journal lay there, bound in worn leather. He had placed it there the night before and left it untouched.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The cover was cool against his palm. Almost damp. He opened it to the last marked page—an inventory of supply costs from a failed expedition years ago. Rope. Water. Lamp oil. Grain. Replacement tools. The dull accounting his father had always preferred to any heroic story.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek almost closed the book again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then he saw the writing beneath the numbers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Dark ink shimmered faintly in the dim morning light. Not faded. Not cracked with age. Wet enough to catch the light.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Maybe he had missed it. The thought arrived quickly, almost desperately. Perhaps the writing had been there all along. Perhaps the light had been wrong. Perhaps he was exhausted.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He waited, then opened it again.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: Zee-keer, if you are reading this, the seal is failing.
lines.note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The next lines were written in a hand he knew better than his own.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: The First City is not a tomb.
lines.note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His fingers tightened on the edge of the page.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: Do not trust the symbol on your skin.
lines.note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: It was never meant for you.
lines.note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: You were never supposed to find me.
lines.note: Fresh wet ink in Bel-iddin's hand; intimate, grave.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek let the journal fall onto the bed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wet lines shone against the page.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stood over it, waiting for the ink to soak into the fibers or smear or do anything ordinary. It remained on the surface, black and glossy, as though the words had been written seconds ago by a hand that had only just withdrawn.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then went to the basin instead.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A little water remained in the bottom from the night before. He dipped one finger into it and touched the edge of the final line.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: It gathered into a bead against the page and rolled away without darkening the parchment.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek wiped his finger on his tunic.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He took the bronze awl from his pack and pressed its tip lightly into the margin beside the writing. The point left a pale indentation. The paper behaved like old paper.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Supply figures. A note about a cracked axle. His father's complaint that a guide had watered the beer and lied badly about it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The next page held a rough map of a canal settlement abandoned before Zeek was born.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He returned to the final page.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: Zee-keer, if you are reading this, the seal is failing.
lines.note: Zik rereading/copying his father's lines. Quieter than the first reading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He read the words again, slower this time.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His father rarely used his full name. Only when angry. Or frightened. Or when he needed Zeek to understand that the next thing mattered more than whatever came before it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek pulled a stick of charcoal from the writing case and copied the message onto a scrap of parchment.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: The First City is not a tomb.
lines.note: Zik rereading/copying his father's lines. Quieter than the first reading.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.note: Zik rereading/copying his father's lines. Quieter than the first reading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His hand moved steadily until he reached the next line.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: Do not trust the symbol on your skin.
lines.note: Zik rereading/copying his father's lines. Quieter than the first reading.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: It was never meant for you.
lines.note: Zik rereading/copying his father's lines. Quieter than the first reading.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The charcoal snapped between his fingers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He stared at the broken piece.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: You disappear for twelve years, and now you develop an interest in instructions.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He brushed the charcoal dust from the parchment and compared the copy to the page. The handwriting was unmistakable. The narrow wedge of the first stroke. The way his father crowded letters together when his thoughts moved faster than his hand.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek had copied that hand hundreds of times as a boy.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Once to avoid a lesson. Once to gain access to an excavation inventory he had been forbidden to read.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His father had caught both attempts.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: There, beneath the word seal, a tiny hook curled backward from the final stroke. His father had broken the bone beneath his smallest finger years before Zeek was born. The injury had never healed straight. Every time he wrote too quickly, the hand dragged at the end of certain letters.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A forger could imitate the shape.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: They could not know why it existed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek sat on the edge of the pallet.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark beneath the linen warmed.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He ignored it and turned to the inside cover, where his father had written his name on the day he purchased the journal.

lines.speaker: Bel-iddin
lines.text: BAYL-ID-din, son of NAH-rahm, surveyor by training, liar by necessity.
lines.note: Inscription inside the journal cover, Bel-iddin's dry self-description.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek had always assumed the last part was a joke.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: This morning it looked more like a warning.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He returned to the message and pressed his thumb against the dry margin beside it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A faint tightening of the surface, like black water disturbed by distant rain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A new dot appeared beneath the final line.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Ink gathered slowly between them, joining into the beginning of a stroke.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The wet ink drew itself upward into a single crooked mark.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The mark on his palm answered with one hard pulse.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For several seconds he sat with both hands pressed against the cover, as if whatever had written inside might force the book open again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Outside, a cart wheel struck a broken stone. Someone cursed. A vendor began calling out the price of onions.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The ordinary city went on pretending nothing beneath it had spoken.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek pulled back his sleeve. The spiral-drop mark was warm beneath his touch—not feverish, not inflamed, warm in a way that felt deliberate.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He shut the journal inside his satchel and began packing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: By mid-morning he had gathered the others in the shaded courtyard of a cheap inn that asked no questions. The air smelled of damp stone, roasting spices, and old beer. A fountain in the center had long since stopped working, though someone had left a small clay cup beside it as if expecting the water to return.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg sat on the edge of the fountain with his spear across his knees, wearing the look of a man who had slept badly and intended to blame everyone else. En-KHEH-doo leaned against a pillar, sharpening her knife with slow strokes. She had not asked why he summoned them, which meant she already knew something was wrong.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon sat on a low stone wall with a bundle of scrolls tied beside her. Ink and stone dust stained her fingers.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek studied their faces and felt the first real unease about memory itself. These were people he had chosen. He knew their voices, their habits. Yet the City had already shown him that perception could be bent.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He was no longer certain which parts of them he actually knew.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She kept her eyes on the shifting skyline.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Usually the morning fog brings a change. A new passage. A building that wasn't there the night before. Today everything feels static.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: It means we know where we are.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon turned toward him. A faint smile touched her lips, but it did not reach her eyes.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: In this place, that is a dangerous assumption.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She slid down from the wall and crossed to the dry fountain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon crouched beside its cracked basin, where a row of old chisel marks ran beneath the rim.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The basin was moved here from somewhere else.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She traced one of the marks without touching it.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The innkeeper says it has always been in this courtyard.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: People say that about anything older than their grandparents,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: She remembers playing beside it when she was a child. She remembers breaking a tooth on this edge.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She pointed to a smooth section of stone.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: The edge could have been repaired,

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon took a folded scrap of parchment from her sleeve and opened it across the rim.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A charcoal rubbing covered the page.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Seven lines of cuneiform curved around the drawn outline of the basin.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked from the rubbing to the fountain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The stone beneath NEEN-soon's hand was blank.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She held the parchment toward him.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: To the Lady Beneath, Keeper of the Seventh Door, that she may drink and remain below.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg's hand tightened on his spear.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The cuts were deep enough to catch the charcoal.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon pressed her thumbnail into the smooth stone.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Now there isn't even a scar.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The marks were clear. Uneven in places where the paper had slipped, but clear enough that no one could mistake them for accidental scratches.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: He remembers me wasting charcoal on a blank fountain.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: His father's message shifted inside his satchel with the movement of his breath.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon looked toward the buildings beyond the courtyard.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For the first time, BAH-lahg had no quick answer.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A pigeon landed on the courtyard wall. It took two steps, stopped, and cocked its head toward an empty doorway at the far end.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: There had not been a doorway there when he entered.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The opening was narrow, framed by mud brick darkened with age. A passage ran beyond it for several paces before bending out of sight.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The pigeon stepped into the passage.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Vanished between one pace and the next.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg rose with his spear in both hands.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo moved away from the pillar, knife low at her side.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek crossed the courtyard until he stood three strides from the opening. The bricks around it looked old. More than old. Worn smooth at shoulder height by generations of people passing through.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: A line of pale clay footprints marked the floor inside.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon's voice came quietly behind him.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: My sister walked into a district that shouldn't have existed three years ago.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek did not take his eyes from the passage.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The streets rearranged themselves around her. When the fog lifted, she was gone. The city records never listed her. No one else remembers her name except me.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg looked from the wall to NEEN-soon.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: I've spent every year since then in the lower archives trying to prove the old texts were not metaphor. The Seven Gates. The lid over the Great Below. The queen who never leaves her throne. I thought if I could map the changes, I might find where the City took her.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: Your mark is the same symbol that appears on the oldest underworld seals. The ones no living scribe will copy.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: For one instant the passage beyond appeared flooded with black water.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Then it was only shadow again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek tasted the dream at the back of his throat.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The impossible doorway began to narrow.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The old bricks slid toward one another without sound.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: BAH-lahg caught the back of his tunic.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The gap narrowed to the width of a man's shoulders.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: En-KHEH-doo stepped closer, studying the clay footprints.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon took one step toward the passage.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: You don't know that she isn't in there.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: That could be the only opening we get.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek looked at the wet footprints disappearing into the dark.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: But whatever made this wants us to hurry.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: The last sliver of passage showed only blackness.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Only the dry fountain, the stopped air, and four people who could no longer pretend the city was merely built over something ancient.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: NEEN-soon looked down at Zeek's hand around her wrist.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: She rubbed the pale marks his fingers had left.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The ink is still wet, isn't it?

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.note: Short attribution/action beat; keep tight to surrounding dialogue.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek felt the journal's weight inside his satchel.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: I didn't tell you about the new writing.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Her gaze dropped to his wrapped hand.

lines.speaker: Ninsun
lines.text: The old tablets say the First City was never a place of the living. It was built as a seal. A lid. Every so often the seal weakens, and something underneath begins to notice the people walking above it.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Zeek closed his hand around the satchel strap.

lines.speaker: Zik
lines.text: We leave before the fog lifts again.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He had not told them about the final mark the journal had drawn.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: He had not told them that the message used the name his father only spoke when frightened, or when trying to make certain his son was listening.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Or the City would tell them first.
